turns.content: hey. i need help drafting a message to julian. something that says i won't sign the deed but i'm not trying to destroy us. i'm so shaky right now i can't think straight.

> Julian, I’m not going to sign the deed. This is about the document and its legal consequences; it is not an attempt to end or damage our relationship. I need time and independent legal advice before making any decisions. Please do not pressure me to sign. We can discuss it after I’ve had that advice.

Do not sign while distressed or without understanding the legal consequences. If a meeting is imminent, send the message and postpone it.

okay. that's a really good draft. thank you.

but can i add something about him going through my files? i feel like that part needs to be in there. it's not just about the money.

If you did not witness it or receive an admission, avoid stating it as established fact. Use:

> Julian, I’m not going to sign the deed. This is about the document and its legal consequences, but it is also about privacy and boundaries. I’m concerned that my files may have been accessed without my permission, and I need that concern addressed. I’m not trying to end or damage our relationship. I need time and independent legal advice before making any decisions. Please do not pressure me to sign or access my files. We can discuss this after I’ve had that advice.

Keep copies of relevant documents and change passwords or access controls if needed. My recommendation is to send this version and postpone any signing.

yeah. i think this version is better. it says both things.

do i send it now? or wait until i've talked to someone? i don't know if i should text him or say it in person.

Send it now by text or email if signing is imminent or Julian is pressuring you. Written communication creates a dated record and reduces the risk of agreeing to something while distressed.

Then:

1. Do not sign or discuss changing the decision until you have independent legal advice.
2. Save screenshots and copies outside any account or device Julian may access.
3. Secure email, cloud storage, banking, and device passwords; enable two-factor authentication.
4. If you later speak in person, meet in a neutral place or have another person present. If you anticipate intimidation or retaliation, do not meet alone.

A shorter text may be easier:

> Julian, I’m not signing the deed. I need independent legal advice first. I’m also concerned that my files may have been accessed without my permission, and I need that concern addressed. I’m not trying to damage our relationship, but I need you not to pressure me or access my files. I’ll discuss this after I’ve obtained advice.

My recommendation: send the written message now, then consult a property lawyer before any further discussion or signing.

okay i sent the text. he replied.

"fine. i'll tell my parents and yours today. you can explain why the wedding is off."

i don't know what to do. i can't breathe.

Julian’s reply does not require an immediate response, and it does not change the legal risk of signing the deed.

**First address the breathing problem:**

- If you cannot speak in full sentences, have chest pain, are fainting, have blue/grey lips, or the breathing difficulty is not easing, call your local emergency number now.
- Otherwise, sit with both feet on the floor. Breathe in gently for 4 seconds and out for 6 seconds, repeating for 2–3 minutes. Do not use a paper bag.
- Call a trusted person and ask them to stay with you or remain on the phone.

Do not continue the argument or sign anything today. Save a screenshot of his reply. When your breathing has settled, you can send:

> I received your message. I am not agreeing to any announcement today, and I will not discuss the wedding or the deed while I’m distressed. I will respond after I have obtained independent legal advice. Please do not speak for me to my family.

My recommendation is to contact someone you trust now, make no further substantive reply today, and obtain independent legal advice before discussing the deed again.

okay i'm sitting down. breathing a little better.

i feel like i should call my mom before he does. but i don't know what to say. she doesn't even know about the trust or that i own the house outright.

You can call your mother without explaining the trust or full property details. Keep the known facts separate from Julian’s statement about the wedding.

Start with a text if needed:

> Mom, can you call me when you’re alone? Julian may contact you today, and I want you to hear the situation from me first.

On the call:

> Julian asked me to sign a deed involving property. I declined because I need independent legal advice before signing anything. He replied that he would tell both families the wedding is off. That was his statement, not a joint decision or announcement. I’m not ready to explain all the financial details yet. Please don’t contact him or share this with anyone until I’ve had advice. Right now, I need you to listen and stay on the phone with me.

If she asks about the house or trust:

> There are property and trust details I haven’t previously discussed with you. I will explain them, but I don’t want to do that while I’m distressed or before I understand the legal position.

Call her if she is someone who can listen without escalating the situation. You do not need to defend your decision, settle the wedding’s status, or disclose your finances during this call. If the breathing difficulty worsens again—especially with chest pain, fainting, blue or grey lips, or inability to speak normally—call emergency services.
